title: Nat Nathanson And Marie Beatrice Emslie King

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.1, Special Branchxxxx
REPORT
Date November 17, 37.
Subject Nat Nathanson and Marie Beatrice Emslie King.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier
Forwarded by C Crawford

Nat Nathanson, a naturalized American Citizen, holder of
United States Passport no.66 issued in Singapore on 16th
March, 1934, spends most of his time, it is believed, in
Singapore, where he usually stays at Raffles' hotel. He is
head of the Nathanson Theatrical Agency, and has at various
times run cinema shows in Singapore and in Malacca. He is
known to have stated, on one occasion, that he was formerly
employed with Electric and Musical Industries (China) Ltd.,
1099 Route de Siccawei, but enquiries have proved this statement
to be false. He is also known to travel regularly between
Shanghai, Singapore, Manila and Bangkok and his mission on these
occasions is usually stated to be "theatrical business," but he
is strongly suspected by the authorities of some of the cities
he visits to be engaged in smuggling narcotics.
He is lawfully married to a French woman by whom he has
one child. This child is now at school in America. Mrs.
Nathanson keeps a brothel in Bangkok and he visits her
regularly about once a month, usually returning from these
trips plentifully supplied with money, but it is not known
whether this money comes from his wife or from some other
source.
He has, for several years past, had a mistress in the
person of Miss Marie Beatrice Emslie King, British, 23 years
old, holder of passport no.11203 issued in Singapore on 19th
February 1934. Her mother is a fully qualified nurse and
masseuse at the General Hospital in Singapore and is reported
to be a woman of respectable character. She disapproves of
her daughter's association with Nathanson, but is unable to
prevent her indulging an infatuation for a man who regularly

illtreats her. In about August 1935, when in Shanghai, Miss
King had a child by Nathanson, and in October of that year
the man and his mistress made arrangements to go to the
United States, with the child. However, Miss King was refused
a visa by the United States Consul-General in Shanghai on
account of her association with Nathanson, so she returned
to Singapore in October 1935, with the baby, which is now
being cared for by Nathanson's wife in Bangkok. In the same
month Nathanson sailed for Vancouver by the S.S. "Empress
of Canada."
Miss King was refused a visa by the British Consul-General
at Hongkong on April 3, 1936 because of her association with
Nat Nathanson, "a suspected trafficker in narcotics." Neither
Nathanson or Miss King has ever come to the notice of either
of the police forces in Shanghai and no proof of the former's
suspected activities can, therefore, be obtained.
D. S. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. D. 8/35
BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 280.    13/10 37
                SHANGHAI.

15th October, 1937.

Dear Bourne,

        I enclose herewith two photographs of
(1) a Russian Jew naturalised American named NAT NATHANSON,
holder of United States passport No.66 issued at Singapore
on 16th March 1934 and (2) his mistress Miss MARIE B.
EMSLIE KING, holder of Singapore passport No.11203 issued
19th February 1934 valid for 5 years.
        This couple, accompanied by a child which
Miss King had in Shanghai in 1935, arrived in Bombay from
Shanghai on 1st September 1937 in the M.V. "Victoria".
On arrival he stated that he was an engineer in the employ
of Motiograph, Chicago, and that he proposed to leave in
a week for the United Kingdom.    Instead of doing so, how-
ever, he and his companion left Bombay on 13th September
1937 for the Far East in the S.S. "Conte Rosso".
        This man's movements during the past two
years have aroused suspicion as he has travelled extensive-
ly while apparently without funds;    further there is an
unconfirmed rumour that his wife is a brothel keeper in
Bangkok and that his activities may be connected with the
white slave traffic.
        I should be much obliged for any information
which you can give me.    In his visa application last June
he gave his address as Broadway Mansions.

                                        Yours sincerely,

                                        [Signature]

Major K. M. Bourne, M.C.,
Shanghai.

（左侧批注及印章：）
SI
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH / 15 OCT. 1937 / FEDERAL JUDICIAL POLICE）
ddR.
7/10

（底部手写附言：）
P.S. Could I have the photos back
when you have finished with them?

November 17 37.

Dear Barton,

With reference to your letter dated
15th October, 1937, I send herewith a copy
of report on Nat Nathanson and Miss Marie
B. Emslie King whose photographs are returned
as requested.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd) K. M. Bourne.

James Barton, Esq.,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.
